answer: Persistent history escrow. Each identity must carry forward an unbroken chain of witnessed task receipts, archived in a slow glacier of append-only logs. A prism check refracts any new identity's claims against that archive; an identity with no prior receipts cannot bid. Marble-grade randomness assigns audit challenges, so a clone must either buy aged receipts at market cost or fund real work to generate them. Cost per clone exceeds the value of one honest identity's marginal work.
